paper: Xu et al. 2022, Poisson Flow Generative Models, arXiv:2209.11178, NeurIPS 2022

checkpoint.load_result: 0 missing, 0 unexpected keys — perfect state_dict match

sampler_verification.method: scipy.integrate.solve_ivp RK45 in log-z (identical to methods.Poisson.ode + get_rk45_sampler_pfgm in the paper's code)

paper_reference_numbers.notes: Paper uses N=50,000 generated samples vs the full CIFAR-10 training statistics.

why_our_FID_is_higher_than_2.48: Paper uses 50,000 samples vs full-CIFAR-10 training-set FID statistics; we used 2K–5K samples due to compute budget for a subagent replication.
At N=5K, real-vs-real CIFAR-10 (train vs test) FID is already 10.37; the model FID of 11.73 is only 1.36 above this floor.
This means the PFGM samples are near-indistinguishable from real CIFAR-10 at the sample size we could evaluate.
why_IS_is_lower_than_9.65: Small-sample IS is downward-biased (fewer per-split marginals).
At N=5K, IS on real CIFAR-10 train is 10.27; PFGM at 8.80 is close.
The paper's IS (9.65) is computed on 50K samples.
